correctness.rationale: For the precise signed orbit of odd weights, the support-function rearrangement formula is exact. A local minimum with two positive magnitude levels would restrict to a local minimum of a positive linear functional on an ellipsoid stratum, contradicting its strict-negative second variation at a stationary point. At each one-level normal the small-angle formula is an exact identity because 0<tan(theta)<1/(2sqrt(k)) fixes the zero/nonzero block order; centered active upper-step vectors give A_k(a)>=sqrt(k(k-1))||a||, and inactive unsigned step vectors give C_m(z)>=min(2m-1,m sqrt(m))||z||, with explicit equality cases. Mixing the orthogonal blocks cannot improve their cheaper sharp coefficient. Comparing integer squares gives a strict switch at k=2m. In chambers the support function is linear, so all maxima are precisely its sphere-gradient directions; perturbing any tie or zero makes it increase. The arbitrary-n proof is independent of checker sampling. All boundary dimensions n=2,k=1,k=n and m=1,2 are included.

originality.rationale: Published type-B signed-majorization and Coxeter-fan results and a separate sharp roundness result provide structural prerequisites, not the complete local-extremum set plus attained directional-angle minimum and threshold of the odd-weight realization. A prior unsigned type-A local-width theorem is not covering: antipodal doubling restricts the type-A objective to a smaller sphere, so critical points and tangent minima do not follow by taking a special case. The two-mode (active tie-splitting versus zero activation) geodesic stability law requires additional calculations and is not implied by facet enumeration alone. Historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The theorem fully classifies spherical width extrema and gives a new exact, attained, all-dimensional local stability law for a canonical signed Coxeter zonotope. The sharp mode change at k=2(n-k) is a structural transition between splitting a tied active block and activating formerly zero coordinates; its coefficient is not contained in standard facet counts or the unsigned type-A theorem. It identifies the abundance and robustness of strict nonglobal minima in a natural nonsmooth geometric optimization landscape. This is motivated by Weyl orbit geometry and fixed-angle width robustness, not an arbitrary slice or minor numerical gain.
